rationale: Both react to TOUCH at t=8 and STARTLE at t=68. Creature A shows narrow focus on PLAY_BALL, briefly shifting to PERSON_ALPHA (t=8–11) and FOOD_TROUGH when offered (t=32–35), but ignores CALL (t=20) and PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL (t=44), then spends a long span with attention NONE (t=40–67, t=72–95) aside from the startle response. Creature B exhibits richer, coherent shifts: starts social, spontaneously moves to FOOD_TROUGH (t=18–19), then PLAY_CHIME (t=30–31), later SEALED_GATE (t=42–43); responds to CALL (t=20), OFFER_FOOD (t=32–41), and PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL (t=44–53); sustains attention to the buzzer (t=68–77) and then initiates PLAY_BOW toward PLAY_BALL without prompt (t=78–83). This indicates greater autonomy, adaptability, and ongoing self-directed activity.
